facts.fact: The US-Mozambique health MOU signed on 15 December 2025 states that the Integrated Electronic Medical Record System (SIS-RME) is owned and operated by the Government of Mozambique, and that data systems the US funds are to be fully led and owned by the Government with US technical assistance and workplan oversight (sections 2.5.1 and 2.5.2).

The MOU states the US Government plans to fund SIS-RME's software development, equipment, the transition of SESP's functions, data-capture improvements and integration into the health data exchange, within US$83,072,079 of data-systems funding over 2026-2030 (US$16,666,385 in 2026); Mozambique commits only to pay ongoing licensing, cloud and hardware costs the US does not pay, and no Mozambican amount is given.

The MOU, running from 1 April 2026 to 31 December 2030, names SIS-RME as the core product of the national digital health platform, with a yearly data-systems funding plan and a Data Systems Roadmap holding its development and deployment detail; a minimum viable version is targeted for September 2026 with modules for registration, consultation, maternal and child health, and HIV and TB services for inpatients and outpatients.

On 15 December 2025 Mozambique and the United States signed an MOU committing Mozambique to implement SIS-RME, with a minimum viable version targeted for release in September 2026, the US-built patient tracking system SESP to pass to Mozambican management by 20 June 2026 and be retired once migrated into SIS-RME, and a scannable data-capture solution for low-burden health facilities by the end of June 2027.
